record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: For β-skeletons with parameter β in the interval [1, 2], determine whether one can prove a stronger lower bound on the spanning ratio that depends explicitly on β.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10. For the range β ∈ [1, 2], is there a stronger lower bound of the spanning ratio that depends on β?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane. For a real parameter $\beta \geq 1$, the β-skeleton of $P$ (in the circle-based / "lune-based" definition) is the undirected graph on vertex set $P$ in which two points $p, q \in P$ are joined by an edge if and only if the open region $L_\beta(p,q)$ — defined, for $\beta \geq 1$, as the intersection of the two open disks of radius $\beta\,|pq|/2$ whose centers lie on the line through $p$ and $q$ at distance $(\beta/2 - 1/2)|pq|$ from the midpoint of $pq$ on opposite sides — contains no point of $P \setminus \{p,q\}$. (At $\beta = 1$ this is the Gabriel graph; at $\beta = 2$ this is the relative neighborhood graph.)

The spanning ratio (stretch factor) of a connected geometric graph $G$ on $P$ is
$$\mathrm{sr}(G) \;=\; \max_{p \neq q \in P} \frac{d_G(p,q)}{|pq|},$$
where $d_G(p,q)$ denotes the length of a shortest path from $p$ to $q$ in $G$ (with edges weighted by Euclidean length), and $|pq|$ denotes the Euclidean distance.

For each $\beta \in [1,2]$, let
$$f(\beta, n) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{\mathrm{sr}(\beta\text{-skeleton of } P) \;:\; P \subset \mathbb{R}^2,\ |P| = n\bigr\}.$$

It is known that $f(1,n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n})$ (Gabriel graphs) and that $f(2,n)$ can be as large as $\Omega(n)$ (relative neighborhood graphs). Determine whether one can establish, for $\beta$ ranging over the interval $[1,2]$, a worst-case lower bound on $f(\beta,n)$ as a function of $n$ that depends explicitly and non-trivially on $\beta$ (i.e., a lower bound that strengthens monotonically as $\beta$ increases from $1$ toward $2$, interpolating between the $\Theta(\sqrt{n})$ bound at $\beta=1$ and the $\Omega(n)$ bound at $\beta=2$).
artifact.status_search_result: Existing results (Bose–Devroye–Evans–Kirkpatrick and related work) establish that the β-skeleton has spanning ratio $\Theta(\sqrt{n})$ for $\beta = 1$ (Gabriel graph) and $\Omega(n)$ in the worst case for $\beta = 2$ (relative neighborhood graph), with a uniform $\Omega(\sqrt{n})$ lower bound for $\beta \in [1,2)$. We did not find a published result giving a sharper β-dependent lower bound that interpolates between these extremes for the full range $[1,2]$, so the explicit β-dependent lower bound problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the Spanning Ratio of Gabriel Graphs and β-skeletons
status_evidence.snippet: For all β-skeletons with β ∈ [1, 2), there exist point sets whose spanning ratio is at least (1/2 - o(1))√n.
status_evidence.claim: A uniform Ω(√n) lower bound is known for β ∈ [1,2), but no β-dependent strengthening is given.

status_evidence.title: Beta skeleton - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Gabriel graph (β=1) and relative neighborhood graph (β=2) are special cases of β-skeletons.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms standard definition framework used in the problem.

status_evidence.title: The spanning ratios of β-Skeletons (Wang, Li)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies spanning ratios of β-skeletons across parameter ranges.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work studies β-skeleton spanning ratios but does not resolve a β-dependent lower bound on [1,2].
